newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 18.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Tuesday:
* H.F. Ahmanson increased its all-stock hostile tender offer for Great Western Financial to $6.6 billion, or about $50 per share.
* The Dow Jones Industrial Average recovered late in the day to close up 20.02 points at 6,955.48 while the Nasdaq index finished down 13.54 point at 1,279.43
* The Securities and Exchange Commission could require mutual funds to reveal their top holdings rather than disclose all the securities they hold to shareholders.
* Advanta said it would post a net loss in the first quarter due to bad loans. The news reflected a larger trend of rising credit card defaults.
* Krupp-Hoesch was planning to start a hostile bid for Thyssen, Thyssen said. Thyssen said it would fight any such move.
* ADT Inc and Tyco International announce friendly $5.4 bilion stock merger.
* If Time Warner keeps its pact with U S West in place through June, it could avoid millions of dollars of capital gains tax.
* News Corp said it would acquire Heritage Media in a non-taxable stock swap valued at $754 million.
* Rockwell International said it would spin off its automotive parts units as a publicly-traded company, in its transformation into a company more focused on electronics.
* Pearson Plc said over the next five years it would invest $160 million in the Financial Times in the United States and Asia.
* Federal investigators find many health maintenance organizations checked by its auditors did not fully meet federal requirements about handling patient appeals.
* The Canadian government said U.S. proposals to toughen air quality standards would "continue to result in health damages and death."
* Luby's Cafeterias said its chairman Ralph Erben quit, and former company chairman John Lahourcade would take his place.
* Rental car agency Avis is facing a lawsuit over discrimation complaints against several of its outlets.
* Ford said it would end production of its Thunderbird car this year.
